 PER PADMA PANDEY,PRESIDING MEMBER
This order will dispose of aforementioned two appeals bearing No. A/126 of 202

5 titled as Pinnacle Resorts Pvt. Ltd., The Khyber Versus Rashpal Singh Dhaliwal & ors and
 appeal No.A/229 of 2025 titled as Evergreen Travels Vs Rashpal Singh Dhaliwal & Ors. both

arising out of one and the common order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the District Consumer

Disputes Redressal Forum-II, U.T. Chandigarh whereby complaint of the complainant-Rashpal

Singh Dhaliwal bearing No.438 of 2023 was partly allowed and the Opposite Parties were

directed as under:-
"i)OPs shall refund the balance amount of Rs.49,000/

 (towards the air tickets) to the complainants in proportionate to their
 payments.
ii) OPs shall refund the amount of Rs.2,81,800/- (towards the booking of hotel
 rooms) to the complainants in proportionate to their payments.
iii) OPs shall pay lump sum compensation of Rs.30,000/- to the complainants
 in equal shares on account of mental agony & harassment including litigation
 expenses.
The above said order shall be complied with by the OPs within a period of 45
 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order failing which OPs
 shall be liable to pay interest @ 9% p.a. of the above mentioned amounts
 thereafter.
2. The facts are being culled out from appeal No.126 of 2025 titled as Pinnacle
Resorts Pvt. Ltd. Versus Rashpal Singh Dhaliwal & ors ;
Before the Ld. Lower Commission, it was case of the complainants that they

planned a tour to Srinagar and in order to avail the booking facility at Srinagar, they

approached Opposite Party No.1. Opposite Party No.1 assured for arranging good tours &

travel and hotels at Srinagar, as such, the complainants booked three Indigo Flights through it

for travelling from Chandigarh to Srinagar for the period of three days i.e. 09.07.2023 to

11.07.2023 by paying an amount of Rs.1,34,000/- on 30.06.2023 towards the air tickets.

Opposite Party No.1 even booked Khyber Gulmarg Orient/3 Rooms 2 Luxury Balcony Room-

Gulmarg View + 1 Luxury Balcony Room-Himalayan View in the Hotel Orient Vacation on
 30.06.2023 for the complainants. Opposite Party No.2 confirmed the booking. An amount of

Rs.2,81,800/- was paid by the complainants towards the hotel booking. As per the schedule,

the flight was supposed to depart from Chandigarh at 7.55 AM and to reach Srinagar at 9.15

AM on 09.07.2023. It was further averred that on 8.07.2023, the complainants came to know

online that the flights would be delayed on 09.07.2023 due to bad weather conditions and

heavy rainfall. As per online portal of the Opposite Parties, the scheduled time for departure

changed from 7.55 AM to 12.30 PM. Due to sudden change in the weather conditions, the

complainants had no other choice but to cancel the said bookings. Accordingly, they contacted

Opposite Party No.1 for cancellation of the bookings and requested to initiate the refund

process. It was further stated that it came to their utter surprise when Opposite Party No.2

vide its email dated 09.07.2023 informed that the weather conditions had been improved and

told the complainants to travel as per schedule. It was further stated that the cancellation of

the flights was beyond the scope of the complainants and they did not willfully or deliberately

cancel the said flight. On 10.07.2023, the complainants sent an e-mail to the Opposite Parties

requesting them to at least initiate partial refund or to change the date of travelling but the

Opposite Parties refused to accommodate the complainants and even told the complainants

that the cancellations/amendment would not be possible as the booking was covered under

non-cancellation window. Even complainants sent another e-mail to the Opposite Parties

informing them about the high alert situation in northern states i.e. Punjab, Haryana, Himachal

Pradesh, Chandigarh, Delhi, Jammu & Kashmir but the Opposite Parties paid no attention to

the request of the complainants. The complainants had paid an amount of Rs.1,34,000/-

towards the air tickets and an amount of Rs.85,000/- was refunded to the complainants and

the balance amount of Rs.49,000/- was not refunded. Even the amount of Rs.2,81,800/-

towards the booking of hotel rooms was not refunded by the Opposite Parties. Alleging

deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part of opposite parties, a consumer

complaint was filed before the District Commission with a prayer to refund the balance

amount of Rs.49,000/- towards the air tickets and Rs.2,81,800/- towards the booking of hotel
 rooms along with interest, compensation for mental agony & harassment besides costs of

litigation.
3. Pursuant to issuance of notice, Opposite party No.1 appeared before the
Learned District Commission and filed its reply. In its written version, Opposite Party No.1
while admitting the factual matrix of the case, stated that it made the payments to Opposite
Party No.2 hotel on receipt of the same from the complainants. It was further stated that on
08.07.2023, there were flood like situation in North India and the complainants were afraid of
travelling to Gulmarg. The Complainants requested to postpone dates in the evening around 8
PM and accordingly opposite party No.1 mailed to Opposite Party No.2 hotel and they
reverted that the weather was fine and that the booking was non-refundable and non-
changeable. The complainants got their flights cancelled in less than 24 hours and airline
refunded money after deducting the airline penalty of approximately Rs.47,000/- and
approximately Rs.87,000/- was refunded. It was further stated that Opposite Party No.2
despite repeated mails did not allow booking modification and did not provide any waiver. It
was further stated that all payments had been made to Opposite Party No.2 and the amount
was forfeited by Opposite Party No.2, hence, Opposite Party No.1 had no role in harassment
of the complainants.
4. Opposite Party No.2 did not appear before the Learned District Commission,
despite service, hence, it was proceeded against ex parte vide order dated 12.03.2024.
5. On appraisal of the complaint, and the evidence adduced on record by the

parties, Ld. District Commission partly allowed the complaint of the Complainants , as noted

in the opening para of this order.
6. Aggrieved against the aforesaid order passed by the Ld. District Commission, both

Opposite Parties filed separate appeals- appeal bearing No.126 of 2025 titled as Pinnacle

Resorts Pvt. Ltd., the Khyber Vs Rashpal Singh Dhaliwal & ors has been filed by Opposite

Party No.2 whereas appeal bearing No. A/229/2025 titled as Evergreen Travels Vs Rashpal

Singh Dhaliwal & Ors. has been filed by Opposite Party No.1 for setting aside the impugned

order dated 25.11.2024.
7. We have heard Counsel for the parties, and have gone through the evidence

and record of the case with utmost care and circumspection.
8. It was contended on behalf of the appellant in Appeal No.126/2025 that the

complainants/respondents had booked 3 rooms in their resorts in Gulmarg Kashmir for 2 days

from 9.7.2023 to 11.7.2023 for which an amount of Rs.2,72,580/- was received from the

respondents. After confirmation of booking of rooms reservation details(Annexure A-5) were

issued which explained booking and resorts terms and conditions, payment details, resort

policies and also contained cancellation and retention policy of the resort. The booking was

made through Evergreen Travels at Chandigarh which also booked flight tickets of the

respondents in Indigo airlines. As alleged in the consumer complaint, on 8.7.2023 due to

heavy rains, the respondents had cancelled the tour and flight tickets on the end moments.

As the flight tickets were cancelled prior to 24 hours for the departure of flights, so after

deducting cancellation charges of Rs.49,000/-, refund of tickets was made by Indigo airlines. It

is stated that after the respondents cancelled their tickets, they tried to contact the office of the

appellant and asked for refund of the booking amount which was denied as it was against

appellant's resort booking policy and the booking was cancelled one day prior to their visit as

the resorts had made arrangement as per demand and that as the resort is situated at almost

above 8800 ft. above sea level in Gulmarg in Kashmir, as such, all arrangement had to be

made well in advance and after sudden cancellation that too one day prior to the visit, it was

very difficult to arrange other guests in the room. It was further case of the appellant that it is

very well mentioned in the terms and conditions of the resort policies that 100% retention will

be charged if booking was cancelled prior to 21 days of the fixed date. It is further case of

the appellant that the Learned District Commission has not considered the fact that the

amount of Rs.49,000/- was forfeited by the airlines and the appellant and proforma

respondent -Evergreen travels cannot be made to pay the said amount to the

respondents/complainant, however, the Learned District Commission has erroneously

fastened liability upon the appellant/Opposite Party No2 and Opposite Party No.1 by

overlooking the said aspect.
9. In Appeal bearing No.A/229/2025 it was contended on behalf of the appellant-

Evergreen Travels that the respondents/complainants had made their bookings through the

appellant and the appellant booked their flight tickets via Indigo Airlines and rooms in the

proforma respondent resort for 9.07.2023 to 11.07.2023. However, the respondents

themselves cancelled the flight booking as there was delay of almost 3 hours due to heavy

raining. The refund amount received from the Indigo airlines after forfeiture charges was

handed over to the respondents. However, the respondents had not impleaded the airlines as

a party in the Consumer complaint. It is pleaded that the appellant acted as per directions of

the respondents and did not keep any money with it but the Learned District Commission

wrongly burdened it by making jointly and severally liable to both the opposite parties.
10. It is admitted case of the parties that air tickets were booked for the

respondents by M/s Evergreen Travels for 9.07.2023. However, due to bad weather and

heavy rains, the respondents made a request to cancel the air tickets and sought refund of the

amount. M/s Evergreens travels refunded the amount whatever was received from the Indigo

airlines. According to the respondents, the amount refunded was less by Rs.49,000/- . It is

case of the appellant-Evergreen Travels that it is running a travel agency and providing air

tickets to the travelers on very marginal commission. On receiving the amount from the

respondents, it provided air tickets and there was no defect in the tickets. Rescheduling in

flight, if any, was on the part of the airline and not on the part of the appellant. Further as and

when any information was received from the airline people regarding rescheduling of

flight/delay, the same was immediately supplied to the respondents/complainants. The request

of the complainants for cancellation of tickets and seeking refund was forwarded to the airline

as the refund of air ticket was to be made by the concerned airline. Whatever amount was

received from the Indigo airlines, the same was forwarded to the complainants, as such, there

was no fault on its part. Further, indigo airlines has not been made a party in the consumer

complaint by the complainants. We do agree with the contention made by the appellant-
 Evergreen Travels. The air tickets were cancelled by the complainants due to delayed flight

and on account of said cancellation, amount was forfeited by the indigo airline. For the

amount which was forfeited by the airlines for cancellation of air tickets, the appellant cannot

be made liable to refund the same to the complainants. Impugned order of the Learned District

Commission to that extent requires modification.
11. It is admitted case of the parties that the complainants had booked rooms with
Pinnacle Resorts Pvt. Ltd., The Khyber for 9th July,2023 to 11th July, 2023. The complainants
made a request for the cancellation of the bookings on 08.07.2023 i.e. one day prior to the day
of booking. Even the complainants, as admitted by the appellant Evergreen Travels, also
requested for partial refund or to allow their booking on alternative dates. Request of the
complainants was denied by the appellant on the plea that it was against appellant's resort
booking policy and the booking was cancelled one day prior to their visit. Further, the resorts
had made arrangement as per demand of the complainants and that since the resort was
situated at almost above 8800 ft. above sea level in Gulmarg in Kashmir, as such, all
arrangements had to be made well in advance. On sudden cancellation, that too one day prior
to the visit, it was very difficult to arrange other guests in the rooms. It was further case of the
appellant that it was very well mentioned in the terms and conditions of the resort policies that
100% retention will be charged if booking was cancelled prior to 21 days of the fixed date.
However, the appellant has not adduced any evidence on record showing that the booked
rooms remained vacant due to the cancellation of rooms by the complainants. Even otherwise,
the rooms were not utilized by the complainants and the same must be utilized by the
appellant as the intimation was given to it that the complainants had cancelled the tour due to
sudden change in weather conditions. In this regard, the Learned District Commission also
rightly observed as under ;
"According to the complainants, due to sudden bad weather

 conditions, which were beyond their control, the bookings

 had to be cancelled.
The version of the complainants is also supported by order dated 09.07.2023
 issued by District Disaster Management Authority, Chandigarh (Annexure C-8
 colly) vide which taking into consideration the heavy rain fall and water logging,
 order and advisories were issued to the general public, private institutions and
 government/semi-government offices in Chandigarh for safety of public.
On the other hand, we find that the OPs have not adduced any evidence
 controverting the version of the complainants. The OP No.2 did not appear to
 contest the claim of the complainants and preferred to be proceeded ex-parte,
 thus, we have unrebutted and uncontroverted version of the complainants which
 is duly supported by affidavits alongwith documents Annexure C-1 to C-8. It
 would not be out of place to mention here that OPs have not adduced any
 evidence on record showing that the booked rooms remained vacant due to the
 cancellation of rooms by the complainants. In the absence of any such record, it
 can be safely presumed that the OPs had utilized the said rooms by providing
 the same to any other customer after obtaining the requisite charges."
12. For the reasons recorded above, both the above appeals are partly accepted and

the impugned order is modified to the extent that appellants in both appeals (Opposite Parties

in the consumer complaint) are not liable to refund the balance amount of Rs.49,000/- towards

the air tickets to the complainants. The remaining part of the order shall remain intact.
13. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, in both the appeals also stand disposed
of.
14. Certified copies of this order be sent to the parties free of charge.
15. The file be consigned to Record Room, after completion.
